Subject: Security and MAP for Redwood evaluation (SOC2/SIG/DPA)

Markus,

Thanks for taking the time to talk last week. Stellarus is working to finalize our vendor evaluation plan and we need a short mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out the security/compliance gates and acceptance criteria so our procurement and infosec teams can greenlight a pilot. Key asks up front: 

- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) + auditor name
- Completed SIG/CAIQ questionnaire or equivalent
- Draft DPA and standard retention windows (we need retention + deletion process for PII)
- Data residency guarantees (we prefer US-only for now)
- A proposed schedule (target: pilot start in ~6 weeks) and acceptance criteria for each gate

Can you send a MAP template with milestones and a proposed delivery timeline? Also attaching a short list of Stellarus security questions to kick things off.

Thanks,

Alice Monroe
Head of Vendor Risk, Stellarus Financial
alice.monroe@stellarus.com
Attachment: stellarus-security-questions-20260921.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security and MAP for Redwood evaluation (SOC2/SIG/DPA)

Thanks Alice — appreciate the clarity. I’ve sketched a short MAP below and attached a formal PDF you can drop into your procurement tracker. High level: 6-week runway to pilot, with clear gates at documentation, DPA, and SOC2/SIG evidence. Proposed milestones: 

1) Week 1 — Documentation & intake: CAIQ link, SOC2 report access, DPA draft sent to Stellarus legal
2) Week 2–3 — Security review: Stellarus runs questionnaire, we provide expanded answers / demos of isolation controls
3) Week 4 — DPA finalization + signatures (DocuSign)
4) Week 5 — Staging pilot (test data, telemetry validation, retention behavior)
5) Week 6 — Acceptance decision (signed off by Stellarus infosec & procurement)

Acceptance criteria (examples): SOC2 Type II available and no outstanding high-risk findings; SIG/CAIQ completeness >= 95% with mitigations for any gaps; DPA executed with agreed retention windows; successful data deletion test in staging.

Attachments I’m including: RWI-MAP-proposal-20260922.pdf (MAP with milestones), SOC2-TypeII-report-2026.pdf (Redwood’s most recent report), and a link to our CAIQ export. Laura (legal) and Marissa (CS) are on copy to help with the DPA and the pilot runbook.

If that looks sensible, can we set an intake call this week to walk through the MAP with your security team? I’m flexible Thursday morning PT.

—
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
Attachment: RWI-MAP-proposal-20260922.pdf (PDF, 92KB); SOC2-TypeII-report-2026.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

Hi Markus — thanks for the MAP and the report. A few follow-ups from our side after an initial read: 

- Retention: Stellarus policy requires a maximum retention of 5 years for financial transaction PII and 1 year for ephemeral generated content unless otherwise required for auditing. We also require the ability to enact account-level deletion requests and an API for data purging.
- Residency: We need the pilot to run in US-only regions and have contractual language guaranteeing no replication outside the US without prior consent.
- SOC2: please confirm the auditor name and the date range covered by the supplied Type II report.
- SIG/CAIQ: we will run the attached questionnaire against your CAIQ export; if there are any items you expect to escalate, flag them now.

Can Laura weigh in on DPA redlines? Also Jordan (copied) will coordinate SLAs and procurement. We are targeting a decision by mid-November but would like the pilot live earlier if possible.

Appreciate it,
Alice
Attachment: (none)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security and MAP for Redwood evaluation (SOC2/SIG/DPA)

Hi Alice — Laura from Redwood legal here. Thanks for the clear asks; below are proposed positions and next steps. I’ve attached a redline of our standard DPA for Stellarus review.

1) Retention windows: Redwood proposes default retention of 365 days for ephemeral inference artifacts (cache, non-billing telemetry) and 5 years for billing/financial transaction logs or where retention is required by law. We will accept a Stellarus-requested retention of 5 years for transaction PII as part of the DPA. We will include an API-based data deletion procedure and a documented SLA for deletion requests (target: 15 business days after validation).

2) Data residency: we can commit to provisioning and isolating the Stellarus deployment in US regions (AWS us-east-1 or us-west-2) and will add contractual language prohibiting replication outside the US without prior written consent.

3) SOC2: the attached SOC2-TypeII-report-2026.pdf covers 2025-06-01 through 2026-05-31; auditor: Clearview Assurance. We’ll provide a signed letter of attestation if required.

4) SIG/CAIQ: we’ve exported our CAIQ and provided a Drive link with evidence artifacts. If you identify items for escalation, please list them and we’ll assign owners.

Next steps I propose: 
- Review attached DPA redline (RWI-DPA-redline-stellarus-20261001.docx) and send back comments by 2026-10-08
- Schedule a technical intake on 2026-10-06 to demonstrate the staging deletion flow and residency controls (Markus/Marissa present)
- Exchange DocuSign envelope for the DPA once commercial terms are agreed

I’m attaching the DPA redline and links to the CAIQ export. Happy to hop on with your legal team if helpful.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
